transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I just feel like I’m crawling out of my skin, you know? Whenever I’m supposed to sit still, like in the radiology suite at work, or even in my college classes. Which, by the way, the seats in my anatomy lecture hall are the absolute worst. They're these tiny plastic things attached to the desks, and I swear they were designed for people half my size. The guy who sits next to me always brings this huge iced coffee and leaves the condensation ring right where I need to put my arm. Anyway, yeah, I've been trying to tough it out for months, just telling myself to sit down and focus, but I still end up pacing around the room, or shifting in my seat constantly, or just finding some random excuse to get up and move. Like, I'll volunteer to go restock the lead aprons just to walk down the hall. Lead aprons are super heavy, by the way, but I'd rather lug those around than sit in that chair for another minute.

I don't know why schools can't just buy normal-sized furniture.
